description: The CLI entrypoint guard at apps/landing/scripts/render-dashboard.mjs:103 (`if (import.meta.url === \`file://${process.argv[1]}\`)`) compares an ES-module URL against a RAW, unresolved process.argv[1]. Node.js does not guarantee argv[1] is an absolute path -- it is exactly what the invoker typed on the command line. Any relative invocation, e.g. `node scripts/render-dashboard.mjs` (from apps/landing) or `node apps/landing/scripts/render-dashboard.mjs` (from repo root -- the normal way a GH Action / cron running from repo root would invoke it), makes `file://${process.argv[1]}` a malformed/relative URL that never equals the absolute `import.meta.url`. The guard silently evaluates false: `main()` never runs, the script exits 0 with ZERO console output and ZERO error, and dashboard.json is never fetched/written. This is exactly the production path S11.1 requires ('in production, from SUPABASE_URL + service role key'). The bug is invisible because nothing throws and nothing is asserted -- it looks like a successful no-op run.
fix: Resolve argv[1] before comparing: `import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'; if (process.argv[1] && path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) { await main(); }`. This is the idiom Node's own ESM docs recommend precisely because argv[1] is not guaranteed absolute.
